statusText: The CME weekend halt covers twenty-one of the twenty-four published hours and holds Tail at the floor of a closed venue, while China's in-line loan prime rate hold becomes the first verified macro print of the new week and resolves one open question ahead of the 22:00Z restart
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is the single hour in this window carrying elevated conditional risk, and is published with Tail 14, still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: China holds its loan prime rates for a sixteenth month in the first verified print of the new week, completing a hawkish central-bank stack alongside the Fed's 16 September hike and the Bank of Japan's move to a 31-year-high 1.25%, while the CME halt leaves twenty-one of twenty-four published hours without a tape
body: Twenty-one of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final three contain the 22:00Z restart and its first two hours. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25 - up 0.59% from a 29,743.00 previous close but 76 points below its 29,993.25 session high, so the last observed futures mark was not a session extreme - and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. Friday's marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run and are unchanged: the cash Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% after the FOMC raised the target range to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September. WTI settled 100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent 103.87, down 0.91%. Three verified developments separate this hour from the last published one, and none of them is an escalation. The first is the only scheduled release to print anywhere inside this window: the People's Bank of China held its one-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and its five-year rate at 3.50% for a sixteenth consecutive month, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey. An in-line hold is a non-event in the narrow sense, but it is genuinely informative here because it was the one scheduled item capable of altering the Asian backdrop before the restart, and it did not. The second is contextual rather than new to the tape but had not been named in the previous assessment: the Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% on 18 September, a 31-year high, on a 7-2 vote with Asada and Sato dissenting. Taken with the Fed's hike two days earlier and Beijing's hold, the picture is a coordinated hawkish turn that was widely anticipated - close to 90% of surveyed economists expected the BOJ move - and that equities absorbed without incident, the Nasdaq-100 closing higher on the day of the expiry. This belongs in Stress and Confidence rather than Tail: it is a known, priced policy backdrop, not an unresolved second information wave. The third is a qualifier on the reference marks themselves. Friday 18 September was quarterly triple witching, the simultaneous expiration of index futures, index options and stock options, which concentrates volume and flow into the closing cross. Friday's settlement prints are therefore partly an expiry artefact, which modestly lowers their value as a guide to where the reopening auction will start, and is one reason Confidence is not lifted further despite the added verification. On the geopolitical side nothing has moved since the previous hour. The Saudi-led coalition's account stands: a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh at dawn was intercepted, and attacks on Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu were described as thwarted, with no casualties and no reported interruption to production or export capacity, even though Reuters video shows an Aramco-branded fuel tank burning near King Khalid International Airport before being extinguished. Yanbu loadings have been suspended since the mid-September pipeline attack in any case. The standing counterweight is unchanged, with CENTCOM reporting Hormuz oil and LNG transits at a six-month high, and Friday's third consecutive lower crude settlement is consistent with easing rather than with a supply shock. The shared cross-asset context file was collected at 01:43Z and is roughly 50 minutes old at this assessment, so it is inside the freshness limit and usable this run, unlike the previous hour where it was stale and discarded. It is partial: the futures and calendar sections failed collection, so it contributes no futures or event evidence at all. What it does carry is latest-session, non-real-time breadth, and that breadth is internally mixed rather than aligned - Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%, semiconductors broadly firm with Micron up 3.92%, Arm up 4.04% and Broadcom up 2.97% against a 5.82% fall in Qualcomm, and the eight megacaps split exactly four up and four down. Under the standing evidence rules that dispersion lowers directional conviction; it is explicitly not treated as live NQ structure and does not raise Tail. Japan's cash equity market is closed Monday through Wednesday for Silver Week, with JPX running derivatives holiday trading, so the Asian sessions immediately after the restart will be missing their largest cash market - a liquidity qualifier scored into restart Stress, not into Tail, since thinner depth lengthens absorption without implying direction. One scheduled item is named for completeness: Monday's effective Nasdaq-100 rebalance lifts the SpaceX weight to about 2.82%, but the mechanical passive flow executed in Friday's closing cross rather than at the restart, so it sits behind the market. A Trump-Xi summit is widely reported for 24 September with no confirmed time, so it is omitted from the verified calendar and named only as a week-ahead checkpoint. Tail is held at 4, the floor of a closed venue, because the current hour offers no mechanism for mean reversion to fail and none of the path amplifiers - shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, extreme-holding, aligned cross-assets - can even be observed without an open tape. Stress eases one point to 25 because the LPR hold removed the single scheduled source of pre-restart uncertainty and resolved in line, partially offsetting the Silver Week liquidity qualifier that remains in place. Confidence holds at 74 rather than decaying to the 73 the previous run projected for this hour: three independent verifications were added and the shared context file is usable again, but the fundamental constraint is unchanged - there is still no live price path, the last tape is more than two days old, and that tape was an expiry.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 for the first twenty slots before stepping down to 4 across the final four hours. Stress opened at 24, eased to a 21 plateau across five morning hours, drifted back through 22, 23 and 24, and reached 26 in the final two hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence peaked at 83 early in the window and decayed steadily to 72 as distance from the Friday tape grew, recovering to 74 in the closing hour as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Twenty-one of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final three contain the restart and its first two hours. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No U.S. macro release falls inside this window; the only scheduled release anywhere in it, China's loan prime rate, has already printed unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50%. The next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 08:00Z, 7 from 10:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 16:00Z, 10 from 19:00Z and 11 at 21:00Z, then reaches 14 across the restart and its first full hour before easing to 13 and 12 - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure, and one that stays inside the low band throughout. The one genuinely observable checkpoint inside the halt is Saudi Arabia's Tadawul session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z, the first market-based read on the Riyadh depot fire now that the coalition has described the Yanbu attack as thwarted. The 22:00Z reopening remains the single hour carrying real conditional risk, and it is qualified by Japan's three-day Silver Week cash closure, which leaves the following Asian sessions without their largest cash venue and lifts restart Stress without implying direction. Those hours are published conditionally as event/whipsaw with no opening structure yet observed, easing to mixed once two-sided trade is assumed to resume. Every published hour maps to EA_ON and no danger window is identified.

forecastDetail.comment: Deepest read of the CME weekend halt. China's LPR held at 3.00% and 3.50% for a 16th consecutive month, the first macro release of the new week and an in-line one. With no venue open there is no mechanism for mean reversion to fail, so Tail stays at the closed-venue floor.

No venue open and nothing scheduled. The in-line Beijing hold leaves the hawkish global stack unchanged rather than extending it, after the Fed's 16 September hike and the Bank of Japan's move to a 31-year-high 1.25% on 18 September. Confidence eases purely on distance from Friday's tape.

Static weekend hour between the LPR print and the Gulf cash open. The Riyadh depot fire still has not been priced by any open market, so no structural read on it is available and the published scores carry forward unchanged.

Tail steps to 5 on the restart-approach schedule rather than on any observation. Friday's verified marks remain the reference: cash NDX settled 29,644.17, up 0.67%, and VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of its daily range.

Last hour before Gulf cash markets are scheduled to open. A calm settled VIX and a Friday close just under the session high describe the prior tape but say nothing about the gap that will price at the 22:00Z reopening, so both are treated as background only.

Saudi Arabia's Tadawul trades on Sunday and is scheduled to open in this hour, the first venue able to price the Riyadh and Yanbu reports. Stress edges up for headline sensitivity around that open rather than for anything observed; a contained regional reaction would be the de-escalating read.
